pharm: Triazene cytotoxic prodrug that, after hepatic activation, alkylates and methylates DNA (and may act as a purine analog), inhibiting DNA, RNA and protein synthesis to produce cell death; given intravenously only.
quick: Melanoma: 2-4.5 mg/kg/day IV x10 days q4wk, or 250 mg/m2/day x5 days q3wk
IV drug; restrict oral intake 4-6 h before dose to reduce vomiting
Avoid; teratogenic and carcinogenic in animals (Category C)
Discontinue breastfeeding (excretion unknown; potential serious harm)
Clearance reduced; half-life prolonged in renal dysfunction; use caution
Boxed - hepatic necrosis/hepatic vein thrombosis can be fatal; caution
summary: Dacarbazine is an intravenous triazene alkylating agent used for metastatic malignant melanoma and, in combination, as second-line therapy for Hodgkin disease. It carries a boxed warning: hemopoietic depression is its most common dose-limiting toxicity, fatal hepatic necrosis with hepatic vein thrombosis has occurred, and it is carcinogenic and teratogenic in animals. Severe nausea and vomiting are very common.
indications: Hodgkin disease as second-line therapy in combination with other effective agents

dosage.d: 150 mg/m2/day IV for 5 days with other agents
375 mg/m2 IV on day 1 with other agents

admin: Reconstitute the 200 mg vial with 19.7 mL Sterile Water for Injection to give 10 mg/mL
May be given as a slow IV push or further diluted in 5% dextrose or normal saline and infused IV
Administer intravenously only; avoid extravasation, which causes tissue damage and severe pain
Restrict oral food intake for 4-6 hours before treatment and give antiemetics to reduce nausea/vomiting
Protect reconstituted/diluted solution from light; store reconstituted vial at 4 C up to 72 hours
Administer under supervision of a physician experienced in cancer chemotherapy
moa: The exact mechanism is not fully established. After hepatic metabolic activation, dacarbazine alkylates and methylates DNA, with three proposed actions: inhibition of DNA synthesis by acting as a purine analog, direct DNA alkylation, and interaction with sulfhydryl (SH) groups. The net effect is inhibition of DNA, RNA and protein synthesis leading to cell death. Its major active metabolite is 5-aminoimidazole-4-carboxamide (AIC).
preg: Avoid. Dacarbazine is teratogenic in rats and rabbits (skeletal anomalies, increased resorptions) and is carcinogenic in animals; it is Pregnancy Category C. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the risk to the fetus, and counsel on effective contraception.
lact: It is not known whether dacarbazine is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a nursing infant, discontinue breastfeeding during therapy.
renal: Renal tubular secretion is the main route of excretion; about 40% of a dose appears unchanged in urine within 6 hours. In renal (and hepatic) dysfunction the half-lives are prolonged. Use with caution and monitor in renal impairment.
hepatic: BOXED WARNING component: hepatic toxicity with hepatic vein thrombosis and hepatocellular necrosis, sometimes fatal, has been reported (about 0.01% of patients), mostly with concomitant antineoplastics but also with dacarbazine alone. Use with caution and monitor liver function; the liver is also the site of metabolic activation.

major: Other myelosuppressive antineoplastics and radiation (additive marrow suppression)
Other hepatotoxic antineoplastics (increased risk of fatal hepatic necrosis)
moderate: Hepatic enzyme inducers (phenobarbital, phenytoin - may alter activation)
interactions.food: Not applicable (IV); restricting oral intake 4-6 hours before a dose reduces vomiting.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid due to additive hepatic and gastrointestinal burden.
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor blood counts and liver function around each cycle.

common: Nausea and vomiting (over 90% with initial doses)
serious: Severe leukopenia and thrombocytopenia (can be fatal)
Fatal hepatic necrosis with hepatic vein thrombosis

monitoring: CBC (WBC, platelets, RBC) frequently during therapy; hold/stop for severe depression
counsel: Severe nausea and vomiting are common but usually improve after the first 1-2 days; antiemetics will be given
A flu-like illness (fever, aches, malaise) may occur after large doses and can last several days
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding (low blood counts)
Report yellowing of skin/eyes or right upper abdominal pain (liver injury)
Avoid sun exposure and use protection (photosensitivity)
Use effective contraception; do not breastfeed during treatment
pk: Cytotoxic effect over the treatment cycle
Biphasic: initial ~19 minutes, terminal ~5 hours (prolonged in renal/hepatic dysfunction)
Store vials refrigerated 2-8 C, protected from light
pearls: Boxed warning: myelosuppression (dose-limiting), fatal hepatic necrosis/hepatic vein thrombosis, and animal carcinogenicity/teratogenicity
Over 90% of patients vomit with initial doses; pre-treat with antiemetics and limit oral intake beforehand
Extravasation causes severe tissue damage - administer carefully IV and watch the site
Hepatically activated to its cytotoxic metabolite; the liver is both the activator and a target of toxicity
A flu-like syndrome can follow large single doses
missed: Dacarbazine is administered by clinicians on a fixed cycle; missed or delayed doses are rescheduled by the oncology team. Patients do not self-administer.
overdose: No specific antidote. Provide supportive treatment and monitor blood cell counts closely; manage marrow suppression and hepatic toxicity as they arise.
